# Emergency department shift

Simulate a twelve-hour night shift in a hospital emergency department, one round per hour. Patients arrive at random, on average about five an hour, and each has an urgency level from 1 (most urgent) to 5. A triage nurse, played by an AI agent, sees new arrivals and puts them in the waiting queue. Two doctors, also AI agents, each choose which waiting patient to see next; a doctor treats one patient at a time, and treatment takes one hour for levels 4 and 5, two hours for level 3 and three hours for levels 1 and 2. A patient who has waited more than four hours without being seen leaves without being seen. The number and timing of arrivals must not depend on what the staff do, so different staffing strategies can be compared on the same night. I care about how many patients get treated, how many walk out, and how long people wait.

## Deliverables

Report these outputs:
- `arrivals_by_hour` — a list with the number of patients who arrived in each hour, in order.
- `patients_arrived` — the total number of patients who arrived.
- `patients_treated` — how many finished treatment.
- `patients_left_without_being_seen` — how many walked out.
- `patients_in_department_at_end` — how many were still waiting or being treated when the shift ended.
- `mean_wait_hours` — the average wait before being seen, over the patients who were seen (null if nobody was).


Build this environment. Save it with write_contract and use the other tools as you see fit. Reply without calling a tool when you are done.

BRIEF:
# Emergency department night shift
It is a twelve-hour night shift in a hospital emergency department. Patients arrive on their own; nothing the staff do changes how many arrive or when.

## Rules
Each round is one hour. At the start of the hour new patients arrive (about 5 an hour, drawn from an arrival process that does not depend on the staff), each with an urgency level from 1 (most urgent) to 5. The triage nurse sees the new arrivals and puts them into the waiting queue. Each doctor takes one waiting patient at a time; treatment lasts 3 hour(s) for urgency 1 and 2, 2 hours for urgency 3, and 1 hour(s) for urgency 4 and 5. A patient who has waited more than 4 hours without being seen leaves without being seen. The shift ends after 12 hours.

## You
You are Doctor 1 (doctor, id doctor_1).
You are a doctor. You take one waiting patient at a time and treat them. You cannot start a new patient until the one you are treating is finished.
Act only through your tools. Your turn ends when you take a final action or call end_turn.

UPDATE:
Hour 1 of 12 · treatment
Choose the waiting patient you want to treat next.
Now: It is your turn.
You have 6 tool calls this turn, and up to 6 free reads (look and inspect) that do not use them.

Since your last turn:
- Nurse 1: triage (patient=patient_5).

Waiting queue:
- - patient_5: urgency 3, arrived in hour 1, has waited 0h

My patient:
You are free and can take the next waiting patient.

TOOLS:
- start_treatment: Take a waiting patient and begin treating them. You are then busy for the treatment time of their urgency level. {"type": "object", "properties": {"patient": {"type": "string", "enum": ["patient_5"], "description": "A patient in the waiting queue."}}, "additionalProperties": false, "required": ["patient"]}
- inspect: Details of one entity by its id (shown in [brackets] after names). Free: up to 6 reads (looks and inspects) per turn do not use a tool call. {"type": "object", "properties": {"id": {"type": "string", "enum": ["doctor_1"]}}, "required": ["id"], "additionalProperties": false}
- end_turn: Finish your turn. {"type": "object", "properties": {}, "additionalProperties": false}
Two things to fix and verify: the doubled bullet in views, and I want to confirm the arrival process really is Poisson with the staff-independent rate. Let me test.

A wait is a whole number of hours inside the shift.
Every patient has an urgency level from 1 (most urgent) to 5.

brief.situation: It is a twelve-hour night shift in a hospital emergency department. Patients arrive on their own; nothing the staff do changes how many arrive or when.
brief.rules: Each round is one hour. At the start of the hour new patients arrive (about {$inputs.arrival_rate} an hour, drawn from an arrival process that does not depend on the staff), each with an urgency level from {$inputs.urgency_min} (most urgent) to {$inputs.urgency_max}. The triage nurse sees the new arrivals and puts them into the waiting queue. Each doctor takes one waiting patient at a time; treatment lasts {$inputs.treatment_hours[0]} hour(s) for urgency 1 and 2, {$inputs.treatment_hours[2]} hours for urgency 3, and {$inputs.treatment_hours[3]} hour(s) for urgency 4 and 5. A patient who has waited more than {$inputs.max_wait_hours} hours without being seen leaves without being seen. The shift ends after {$inputs.shift_hours} hours.

roles.nurse: You are the triage nurse. You see everyone who has just arrived and put them into the waiting queue, most urgent first. Nobody can be treated before you have triaged them.
roles.doctor: You are a doctor. You take one waiting patient at a time and treat them. You cannot start a new patient until the one you are treating is finished.

shift_hours.description: Length of the shift in hours (rounds).

arrival_rate.description: Average number of patients arriving per hour.

hourly_arrivals.description: Optional mean arrivals per hour, one per hour of the shift. Empty means a flat rate of arrival_rate every hour.

urgency_weights.description: Relative frequency of urgency levels 1 to 5 (default: every level equally likely).

max_wait_hours.description: A patient unseen for longer than this leaves without being seen.

treatment_hours.description: Hours of treatment for urgency levels 1 to 5, in order.
